title: Route budget manifest & SDK sketch
content:
Notes to self - high-level goal:
Make it trivial for developers to declare per-route or per-interaction token budgets (soft + hard) with fallbacks, and expose a small SDK + YAML manifest so infra can enforce and telemetry can attribute costs.

Why:
- Customers keep asking for predictable budgets per feature (chat, summarize, search) so they can guarantee latency/cost SLAs for paid tiers.
- We already have routing, batching, and session-crediting; missing piece is a developer-facing manifest + runtime enforcement that maps nicely to billing and autoscaling hints.

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
- Declarative: devs write a short manifest (route name -> budget profile).
- Pluggable: SDK can be used server-side or in serverless handlers; manifest can live in repo or in Console.
- Signal-preserving: budgets should optionally trigger graceful degradations (shorter responses, lower-fidelity model), not just hard rejects.
- Telemetry first: every request annotated with budget-id, intended budget, actual tokens consumed, fallback path.
- Experiment-friendly: enable A/B of budget profiles with rollout flags.

Persona / user stories:
- As a backend engineer, I want to attach a 120-token soft budget and 400-token hard budget to /api/v1/compose so that front-end product tiers don’t blow past quotas.
- As a growth PM, I want to try a cheaper budget for new users (+ fallback to higher-fidelity model on error) so we can measure retention impact.
- As SRE, I want the runtime to emit per-budget queue latency percentiles so capacity planning can map to budget usage.

Budget semantics (proposal):
- soft_budget: target tokens for good UX. Hitting soft_budget -> signal to runtime to prefer concise responses or lower-cost model variant (policy).
- hard_budget: absolute max tokens allowed before abort or switch to a stubbed response.
- penalty_window: timeframe to accumulate tokens (per-request vs per-session options).
- priority: numeric priority for scheduling when capacity constrained.
- fallback_chain: ordered list of fallback actions (truncate, switch-model:model-small-q4, respond-with-summary, return-429-with-prescription).

Rough manifest (YAML-first) example:
---
budgets:
  compose_api:
    routes: ["/api/v1/compose", "compose:mutation"]
    soft_budget: 120
    hard_budget: 400
    penalty_window: request
    priority: 50
    fallback_chain:
      - type: truncate
      - type: switch_model
        model: redwood-small-q4_8bit
      - type: refuse
        code: 429
        message: "response budget exceeded: consider upgrading"

SDK sketch (JS pseudocode):
// server handler
import { Budget } from '@redwood/inference-sdk';
const profile = Budget.load('compose_api'); // from repo manifest or console
app.post('/api/v1/compose', async (req, res) => {
  const ctx = Budget.startRequest(profile, { userId: req.user?.id });
  try {
    const resp = await RedwoodApi.generate({ prompt: req.body.prompt, ctx });
    await ctx.recordConsumption(resp.tokens);
    res.json(resp.output);
  } catch (err) {
    const decision = await ctx.onError(err); // might trigger fallback_chain actions
    // surface graceful message, log telemetry
    res.status(decision.code || 500).send(decision.message || 'internal');
  }
});

Runtime enforcement notes:
- Enforcement should be local to the serving node to avoid roundtrips. Node caches manifest + fallback policy.
- For streaming, if soft_budget exceeded mid-stream, runtime should switch model or append a trailer advising truncation.
- We must not drop tokens silently — consumer-visible reason codes are important for debugging.

Telemetry and metrics to emit:
- budget_id, route_name, request_id, user_tier
- intended_soft_budget, intended_hard_budget, tokens_requested_estimate, tokens_consumed
- fallback_taken (enum), latency_p95_by_budget, queue_time_ms
- per-budget burn-rate: tokens/sec aggregated 1m/5m intervals

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Developer can declare a manifest and attach to a route (repo or Console).
- Runtime enforces soft and hard budgets for request-scoped budgets.
- SDK provides startRequest/recordConsumption simple surface.
- Console shows per-budget token consumption and a sample of fallback events.
- E2E test for streaming switch model on soft_budget exceed.

Experiment matrix / early hypotheses:
- H1: 10% reduction in median cost per request for routes with soft budgets and switch-to-small fallback, with <5% drop in task success on PRD tasks.
- H2: Showing explicit "budget exceeded" UX increases upgrade conversion vs silent truncation.

Edge cases & open questions:
- How to handle multi-tool/function calling where token consumption is outside of the model runtime? (record custom counters?)
- Session-scoped budgets vs request-scoped: session makes sense for chat but needs rolling-window semantics + decay.
- Interaction with autoscaling: can budget profiles emit autoscale hints (expected tokens/sec) to Dedicated scheduler? Probably yes, sketch separate field "autoscale_hint" with qps and tokens/sec.
- Security: manifest ownership and who can edit in Console; need audit logs.

Prototype plan (2-week sprint):
1) Implement manifest parser and local cache in runtime (edge: 2 days).
2) Add soft/hard enforcement hook and fallback runner (3 days).
3) Build tiny JS SDK (start/record/complete) and sample repo integration (3 days).
4) Wire minimal Console row for per-budget consumption (2 days).
5) Smoke tests and streaming switch-case e2e (2 days).

Next steps / TODOs:
- Sync with infra on model-switch latency and whether switching model mid-request is feasible for streaming paths. (ask: infra/serving-runtime)
- Confirm telemetry schema and sample event size impact. (ask: observability)
- Mock UX copy for "budget exceeded" flows and see legal & support implications. (ask: PM & CS)
- Write a short experiment proposal and include guardrails for user-visible degradations.

Random ideas to jot down:
- Offer a Console toggle to auto-generate budget suggestions from 7-day token percentiles for a route.
- Provide a "budget simulator" in Console to replay a week's traffic and predict fallback counts and cost savings.
- Allow the manifest to reference eval prompt-sets so we can simulate quality impact when switching to cheap models.

Quick sketch of a budget event payload (for telemetry):
{
  "budget_id": "compose_api",
  "route": "/api/v1/compose",
  "user_id": "u-123",
  "soft_budget": 120,
  "hard_budget": 400,
  "tokens_consumed": 225,
  "fallback": "switch_model:redwood-small-q4_8bit",
  "timestamp": "2025-03-02T14:18:00Z"
}

Signing off — this is rough, want to iterate with Mira on SDK ergonomics and with SRE on metrics.
